scenarios.label: Owner, a full day
scenarios.proves: The complete owner view: real attention, real events, real responsibility, and analytics that earned what they claim.

scenarios.label: Owner, a quiet day
scenarios.proves: A genuinely quiet Today, an empty Inbox and light My work, with Analytics that stays honest instead of filling the space.

scenarios.label: New, nothing yet
scenarios.proves: No Project, no history, and genuine setup and unsupported states rather than four empty boxes.

scenarios.label: Collaborator, one project
scenarios.proves: One selected Project and a narrower set of actions, with the narrowing visible rather than inferred from a role label.

scenarios.label: Guest, limited
scenarios.proves: Permission-limited names, counts, evidence and mutations, each disclosed with its shortfall instead of quietly trimmed.

scenarios.label: Partial coverage
scenarios.proves: One source answered for part of its scope. No false zero anywhere, and no reassurance offered in place of the missing part.

scenarios.label: Stale read
scenarios.proves: Data past its freshness threshold, described by when it was last read rather than as current.

scenarios.label: Permission revoked mid-session
scenarios.proves: A Project visible in the list is revoked before the detail read, and not one byte of its metadata survives the transition.

scenarios.label: One provider down
scenarios.proves: One Project could not be read at all while the others stay truthful. Never a global outage, and never a zero.

scenarios.label: No earned trend
scenarios.proves: No trend is drawn, no flat line, no single point, no greyed axis. The words, the gap and the earliest possible date instead.

scenarios.label: A source action fails
scenarios.proves: A source mutation is refused, the event stays open, the optimistic UI rolls back visibly, and recovery is offered.

scenarios.label: Eighteen projects
scenarios.proves: Eighteen Projects, fifty grouped events, sixty responsibilities, long and translated names, and pagination that stays stable.

scenarios.label: The clocks go back
scenarios.proves: Date grouping and snooze resurfacing across a Europe/London clock change, on the one night a fixed millisecond offset is wrong.
